destination.title: Entropy bounds and information limits in cosmology and quantum systems
destination.question: Under which physical assumptions, entropy definitions and observational restrictions do proposed entropy bounds or information limits hold, fail or constrain cosmological and quantum systems?
destination.summary: A proposed navigation family centered on cosmological entropy bounds, their quantum corrections and independent entropy calculations. Adjacent questions about dynamical rates, sensing precision, information geometry, gravitational probability measures and bound-state size remain separately accessible.

systems: Cosmological spacetimes with source-specific dimensions, matter content and cosmological constants
Quantum fields, finite chains, bipartite systems and thermal quantum mechanics
Cosmological horizons and proposed holographic descriptions
targets: Observable entropy and conditional finite-state interpretations
Entropy restrictions on cosmological evolution and vacuum energy
Entanglement and thermal-entropy estimates under specified assumptions
regimes: Positive, zero and negative cosmological constants remain distinct
Expansion, contraction, reheating and postbounce comparisons remain distinct
Classical, semiclassical and explicitly proposed quantum corrections
assumptions: Each source's entropy prescription, matter restrictions and dynamical assumptions remain local to that question
A conjecture or announced result is not treated as an independently verified theorem
conventions: Observable, horizon, matter, generalized, entanglement and thermal entropy are not interchangeable
Finite entropy does not by itself establish the proposed physical Hilbert-space interpretation
Counterterm, energy, mass and field-coordinate conventions must be retained
includes: Tests and counterexamples as well as proposals
Explicit alternate homes for neighboring numerical candidates
excludes: A universal entropy bound inferred from numerical proximity

sources.title: Unbounded entropy in space-times with positive cosmological constant

evidence.text: Does fixing a positive cosmological constant bound every observer's accessible entropy by the entropy of de Sitter space, permitting a universal finite-dimensional Hilbert-space description? The paper tests this using flux-supported product spacetimes.

evidence.text: Can locally asymptotically de Sitter spacetimes with NUT charge violate the four-dimensional entropy bound S ≤ πℓ² and maximal-mass conjecture, including in thermodynamically stable parameter ranges?

evidence.text: Can a generalized uncertainty principle (GUP) heuristically modify Schwarzschild–de Sitter horizon thermodynamics so as to select a probable vacuum-energy fraction, explain a small effective cosmological constant, and connect entropy bounds?

evidence.text: Can cosmological horizons admit distinct, physically motivated energy and mass definitions, consistent thermodynamics, and entropy bounds based on energy inside a bounded de Sitter region?

evidence.text: Estimate horizon-mediated R violation using a massive-particle round trip and a random walk over horizon degrees of freedom, then seek a self-consistent vanishing mass at infinite dS radius. The source explicitly presents this as a heuristic mechanism.

sources.title: Inflationary Implications of the Covariant Entropy Bound and the Swampland de Sitter Conjectures

evidence.text: Reduce the flux action to an oscillator-like quadratic functional, evaluate a flux transition path integral, and use Euclidean-time methods to obtain an entropy and its time derivative.

sources.title: IR/UV mixing, towers of species and swampland conjectures

evidence.text: Solve a provisional species equation, test the next gap against its cutoff, and update the effective count whenever another tower is populated. Repeat in increasing gap order to determine the asymptotically relevant spectrum.

sources.title: Thermal entropy in Calabi-Yau quantum mechanics

evidence.text: The unbounded-entropy argument combines monotonicity with S(T)>log Z(T). Infinite-dimensionality makes Z(T) diverge as T increases without bound, under the assumed existence of the thermal partition function at every finite temperature.

sources.title: Information-theoretic constraints in quantum gravity and cosmology

evidence.text: Constrained extremization introduces Lagrange multipliers enforcing a specified bulk domain. Candidates include interior extremal surfaces and certain boundary-supported global minima; the smallest-area candidate is selected.

sources.title: Unbounded entropy in space-times with positive cosmological constant

evidence.text: Compute product-horizon entropy from one quarter of its area, compare its ratio to empty D-dimensional de Sitter entropy, and examine large-black-hole and near-Minkowski limits.

sources.title: Holography in radiation dominated universe with a positive cosmological constant

evidence.text: Can the holographic relation between closed radiation-universe Friedmann equations and Cardy–Verlinde entropy survive a positive cosmological constant, and can a moving brane in Schwarzschild–de Sitter space realize saturation of the proposed entropy bound?

sources.title: Positive vacuum energy and the N bound

evidence.text: Does every universe with a positive cosmological constant obey an observable-entropy bound S ≤ N = 3π/Λ, including matter-dominated and recollapsing universes that never approach de Sitter space?

sources.title: Entanglement entropy and 2-D black holes

evidence.text: Can vacuum entanglement across a brick-wall partition explain black-hole entropy in a solvable 1+1-dimensional scalar-field model, and what can finite oscillator chains establish before taking a large-N limit?

sources.title: Average entropy of a subsystem

evidence.text: What is the average von Neumann entropy of the smaller subsystem of a bipartite quantum system in a random pure state, and how much information remains accessible within that subsystem rather than in correlations?

sources.title: Black holes and entropy

evidence.text: Can filtering maintain short wavelengths while making the radiation entropy per unit energy arbitrarily large?

sources.title: Role of the cosmological constant in the holographic description of the early universe

evidence.text: How should a positive cosmological constant enter holographic bounds for a radiation-dominated universe: as geometric entropy, vacuum energy, or a parameter of an elliptic-curve description?

sources.title: An area law for one-dimensional quantum systems

evidence.text: How much entanglement can occur across a cut in the unique ground state of a finite one-dimensional chain when interaction range, interaction strength, and the excitation gap are controlled?

sources.title: Holographic cosmology and its relevant degrees of freedom

evidence.text: Can a global, time-symmetric modification of the Fischler–Susskind bound become viable and stringent in four-dimensional cosmologies with zero cosmological constant by counting history-compatible states rather than instantaneous entropy?

sources.title: Quantum gravity in de Sitter space

evidence.text: What asymptotic construction can characterize quantum gravity in de Sitter space, and what could finite entropy imply for quantization, the physical Hilbert space, and precisely calculable or measurable quantities?

sources.title: Entropy and Black Holes in the Very Early Universe

evidence.text: What early-universe history follows from the Covariant Entropy Principle and statistical mechanics when initial conditions maximize probability subject to long-lived localized excitations and an asymptotically de Sitter universe?

evidence.text: Can a classical vacuum be represented as a fixed point of the proposed entropy flow? The author imposes dN/dE=0 at finite E_c and separates finite-entropy and infinite-entropy possibilities.

sources.title: Entanglement entropy of cosmological perturbations for S-brane Ekpyrosis

evidence.text: How much momentum-space entanglement do gravitational nonlinearities generate between sub- and super-Hubble scalar modes during ekpyrotic contraction, and does requiring this entropy to remain below postbounce thermal entropy constrain the S-brane bounce scale?

sources.title: Holography and cosmology

evidence.text: How should the holographic entropy bound be formulated in cosmology, and what conditional restrictions would it impose on expansion, the equation of state, and spatial curvature?

sources.title: Unitary paradox of cosmological perturbations

evidence.text: Assuming a unitary cosmological-horizon description and a thermodynamic interpretation of its area entropy, when does the estimated entanglement between superhorizon and subhorizon curvature modes exceed the proposed entropy bound?

sources.title: Entropy bounds and dark energy

evidence.text: Can entropy bounds make quantum vacuum-energy corrections finite and naturally reproduce the reported dark-energy density while satisfying cosmological equation-of-state constraints? What follows if the resulting length dependence also applies to smaller systems?

sources.title: Holographic entropy bounds in the inflationary universe

evidence.text: Which holographic entropy bounds can describe slow-roll inflation, reheating and the subsequent radiation era, modeled respectively using de Sitter space, radiation with positive cosmological constant and radiation alone?

sources.title: The Entropy of the microwave background and the acceleration of the universe

evidence.text: If cosmic acceleration comes from a positive cosmological constant, is the microwave-background entropy measurable by a local observer bounded parametrically below the entropy of empty de Sitter space?

sources.title: Notes on quantum corrections of swampland and trans-Planckian censorship conjectures

evidence.text: Can quantum entanglement corrections substantially relax cosmological restrictions inferred from entropy and higher-dimensional energy conditions? The paper compares an inflationary Hubble bound with positive-potential gradient bounds, using the same schematic entropy coefficient in distinct constructions.

destination.summary: The 2026 sources report momentum-suppressed threshold rates and challenge earlier fast-cascade estimates. Their amplitude domains and cosmological applications differ; flat-dimension exclusions do not establish exclusion of every warped model.

regimes: Near threshold with comparable daughter masses
assumptions: The broad amplitude claim is bounded by the stated diffeomorphism-invariant two-derivative scalar–gravity setting and treatment of fields and branes.
The irreducible-population constraint uses the stated freeze-in history and reheating bounds.
The earlier s-wave estimate is a rejected comparator in these sources.
conventions: Distinguish daughter momentum from parent mass.
Distinguish a partial decay rate from a summed cascade history.
The freeze-in constraint does not require KK gravitons to constitute dark matter.
excludes: A universal no-go for all gravitational interactions or compactifications
Certification of the announced general proof
Importing the unsupplied companion-paper analysis of warped viability

sources.title: A Universal Kaluza-Klein Graviton Cascade Rate

evidence.text: Uses Gauss–Codazzi decomposition, background Einstein equations, Israel junction conditions and GHY boundary cancellations to obtain the graviton action. A Weyl transformation maps non-minimal scalar couplings to Einstein frame and absorbs their background effect into the warp factor.

sources.title: Near Threshold Kaluza-Klein Graviton Decays and the Dark Dimension

evidence.text: Bound cascade overlaps using profile completeness, then sum daughter channels. For cosmology, sum decay photons over the freeze-in tower, include survival and redshift, and compare bin-integrated signals with archival Galactic and isotropic gamma-ray spectra.

sources.title: A Universal Kaluza-Klein Graviton Cascade Rate

evidence.text: Expands the action to cubic order, applies on-shell mode equations and integration by parts, and sums massive-spin-2 polarizations. Large-mode WKB overlaps and zeta-function channel sums supply the tower scaling estimates.

sources.title: Near Threshold Kaluza-Klein Graviton Decays and the Dark Dimension

evidence.text: Express the surviving three-graviton vertex as the square of a color-stripped Yang–Mills vertex. Use massive transverse-traceless polarization sums for the width and a parent-rest-frame partial-wave argument for its threshold behavior.

sources.title: Near Threshold Kaluza-Klein Graviton Decays and the Dark Dimension

evidence.text: Expand the gravitational action to cubic order and integrate profile-gradient overlaps by parts using the mode equation. On shell, L_□ cancels L_m. The field redefinition h=e^H−1 gives an alternative explanation of their removal.

destination.title: Contested EFT matching of Dark Dimension vacuum energy
destination.question: Can the proposed relation Λcc ∼ mKK⁴ be matched consistently to compactified EFT vacuum energy once radius dependence, cutoffs and UV-sensitive terms are treated?
destination.summary: The supplied sources take opposing positions. One recovers the proposed scaling with a KK-scale cutoff; the other argues that UV-sensitive terms leave the low-energy matching problem unresolved. The excerpts do not adjudicate the dispute.

assumptions: The Dark Dimension scaling is the proposition under test.
The admissible cutoff and dimensional matching prescription are contested.
conventions: Separate Λcc from the UV cutoff.
Distinguish a cutoff at mKK from the species-scale cutoff.
The explicit Scherk–Schwarz calculation uses a compact circle; its authors qualify the circle/orbifold choice.
excludes: Settling the dispute from introductory excerpts
Equating a cutoff substitution with a verified complete EFT matching calculation

destination.question: Could a residual de Sitter α-vacuum generate observable UHECRs, what bound follows on its vacuum parameter, and what would saturation predict?
destination.summary: The 2003 proposal obtains production through matter that breaks de Sitter invariance and considers a saturated-bound explanation of super-GZK events. It is an alternate production mechanism, with no supplied Dark Dimension premise.

regimes: Present-era approximation H = H0 in the source's model
assumptions: Ordinary matter provides the de Sitter symmetry-breaking perturbation.
The source uses a simplified scalar-field model.
Explaining super-GZK events additionally assumes saturation of the inferred bound.
conventions: α denotes a vacuum parameter, not the distance-conjecture exponent.
An invariant vacuum alone is not assigned a nonzero invariant particle flux.
includes: Comparison with decaying superheavy halo dark matter
excludes: Present-day observational validation
A Dark Dimension or KK-tower identification

sources.title: Probing the dark dimension with Auger data

evidence.text: The reviewed arrival-direction analysis uses an unbinned likelihood with directional exposure, a weighted von Mises–Fisher source distribution, and an isotropic background. Its likelihood-ratio statistic tests isotropy; scanning the energy threshold incurs a Monte Carlo estimated trial penalty. This supplies context for the source selection.

sources.title: Probing the dark dimension with Auger data

evidence.text: The authors maximize an energy likelihood, expressed as a product of normalized spectra above a threshold, fitting γ and Ec separately in 20° windows around NGC 4945, NGC 253, M83, NGC 1068, and NGC 891. They report marginalized 68% parameter intervals and display 68% and 95% contour regions.
